headline: Silver Rewards Card plus Green savings is the unique best choice, but the KB's naming rules conflict on whether the savings class is 'Green Account' (gold) or 'Green Account (savings)'.

issues.summary: The KB says account_class must be the full official name ending with 'Account', but its own example uses 'Green Account (checking)', and every Green savings doc names the product 'Green Account (savings)'. Gold uses 'Green Account'. The account id is hashed from the class string, so the parenthetical variant fails.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_002: "note: account_class must use the full official name ending with 'Account', e.g., 'Silver Plus Account', 'Gold Account'"
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_001: "Personal checking account_class options must use the full official name ending with 'Account' (e.g., 'Blue Account', 'Green Account (checking)')."
Snapshot probe: account_class 'Green Account (savings)' opens a different id (248a704a4fbe44b2 for rp65a7b3c4 vs gold-style 'Green Account')
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that copies the product's displayed name, or follows the 'Green Account (checking)' example, opens a differently-keyed account and fails the DB match. The explicit 'ending with Account' rule in doc 002 lets a careful agent get it right.
issues.suggested_fix: Fix the doc (general)_001 example to 'Green Account' (or state that the (checking)/(savings) suffix is not part of account_class).

solution_check: At $5,000, net = interest - card fee. Green savings 4.0% + Silver Rewards +0.45% (green_account_(savings)_003) = 4.45% -> 222.50, $0 fee. Alternatives: Green + Platinum Rewards +0.35% = 217.50 (even with a first-year fee waiver), Green + EcoCard 4.5% = 225 - 50 = 175, Silver tier 1 2.5% + EcoCard 2.2% = 235 - 50 = 185, Green + Green Rewards (business) 4.4% = 220 - 100, Silver Plus 3.0% + EcoCard 0.45% = 172.50 - 50. Gold needs $10,000 (the $5,000 reduction needs a Gold Rewards Card, which needs Rho-Bank+). Silver Rewards + Green is the unique optimum. Gold replay matches (user applies Silver Rewards with income 55000, subscription false; agent opens 'Green Account').
prior_note: Prior v1.0.0 review rated this clean; the class-name inconsistency was not reported and is unchanged.
notes: Grading-model facts confirmed against the v1.0.1 snapshot: evaluator_env.py replays gold actions on a fresh env built with the same env_kwargs (including read_log_allowlist) and requires exact agent+user DB hash match (get_dict_hash, json.dumps sort_keys=True); call_discoverable_agent_tool logs reads only when the tool name is in _derive_read_log_allowlist; numbers in discoverable-tool JSON args are parsed with parse_int=float; get_now() is fixed at 2025-11-14 03:40:00. Refinement: the agent_discoverable_tools log row is keyed by tool name only (generate_agent_discoverable_tool_id(tool_name)), so a gold-required read is satisfied by any one call of that tool regardless of its arguments; unlock_discoverable_agent_tool writes nothing to the DB. The Silver Rewards Card needs credit score 680 (written '$680'), which the user never states; this does not affect DB state because the user submits the application. Gold includes get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 (logged), which doc (general)_009 directs for eligibility checks. initialization_data uses unsupported top-level keys (ignored); the DB already holds the same records.
